note: Written by tools/payo_assemble.py from tools/payo_assemble_data.py: the map ASSEMBLED from the approved single pieces (ArtSource/payo/pieces-approved-2026-10-12 and the same builders' later pieces). Unity axes. Positions are (x, y up, z north); yaw is degrees clockwise from above.
axes: EVERY PIECE IS A PLAIN glTF (y up, +z its front), copied unchanged. glTFast shows a glTF point (x, y, z) at Unity (-x, y, z): at yaw 0 a piece's FRONT faces +z (NORTH, the valley) and its glTF +x side is on the WEST. Place a piece at `position` with rotation (0, yaw, 0) and uniform `scale`: front = (sin yaw, cos yaw) in (x, z). The meshes made by the assembly (payo_land_*, payo_pit_floor) and the kept far pieces are already turned: place them at the origin with yaw 0. TEST (tools/payo_assemble.py axis, Logs/payo/assembly/axis_test.png): gate_portal at (0, -6, -49) yaw 0 has its stair toward the court and its sun disc facing north; house_shrine at (44.5, -6, 0) yaw 270 has its long stair toward the pit (west); block slabE with yaw 180 has its stepped carving on the EAST (outer) side, and stair_E with yaw 180 descends toward +x.

blocks_note: ONE MODEL PER BLOCK ID (the four corners share monolith). A model's origin is the centre of its block's COLLISION TOP and its top face is AT the origin: place it at (x, top - 0.01, z) WITH ROTATION (0, yaw, 0) -- the yaw is new and it matters: slabE, slabW, midE, bridgeE and most stones need their half turn or their carving faces inward, and BOTH STAIRS need yaw 180 or the ramp descends the wrong way under its collider. `extension` is a plain 40 m shaft with the same origin and yaw, starting 12.6 m down: hang it on the block so a raised block shows no foot. Where a layout makes a block a stair, draw `stair.model` (yaw `stair.yaw`) instead.
movers_note: Origin at the centre of the slab's top; place 1 cm under the collider's top at the mover's current (x, y, z).
pads_note: Origin on the floor at the layout's (x, y, z). pad_speed's travel is its +z: yaw 0 for +z, 180 for -z, 90 for +x, 270 for -x (unchanged: glTFast keeps z).

night.note: By day HIDE the nodes named in `nodes_lit_at_night` that end __flame (they are separate meshes inside fire_bowl, torch and hearth_pot) and draw __lantern and every *_glow material dim; from half time show the flames (breathe them), give each entry of `lights` a warm point light, and raise the emission of the glow materials (the turquoise inlay of the gate and the stage, the houses' windows). There is no separate flame placement any more and no group 'night'.

sky.note: Variant A (peeking; the moon is the eye she lost) as three cut-out layers 16 m apart, tiles of one 2048 atlas: top left hair and stars, top right the figure, bottom left the near arm. It stands 2.9 km out over the valley, beyond the last range: the far clip must reach 3.6 km, or scale the model about the can (the origin) and it subtends the same. Draw it unlit, alpha blended, without fog, BEHIND the far ranges, so the last range covers where her arms fade. Variants B and C are mayari_b_albedo.png and mayari_c_albedo.png, whole pictures for one quad.

life_note: MODELS FOR THE GAME TO MOVE, each standing where it should begin, in the cast's manner (box heads, block bodies; all colour is vertex colour on py_flat and py_weave). They are rigid single meshes with no bones: sway, bob, slide or swap them as the other maps' ambient life does. `do` says what each should do. They are NOT in `placements`. Kinds: villager_stand, villager_watch, villager_carry, villager_plant, villager_sit, child_wave, carabao_stand, carabao_wallow, chicken, chicken_white, dog, egret, hawk. (2026-10-12 assembly: the 60 entries keep their kinds and models and stand on the new land: villagers and animals in the houses' yards, planters, egrets and the wallowing carabao in the nearer paddies, hawks over the valley.)

catch.pivot: the body's origin is under its belly between the talons; it flies along local +Z in Unity (local -Y in Blender); each wing node's origin is its shoulder: flap by rotating the wing about its local Z (the body's long axis)
catch.note: talons hang 1.6 m under the origin: hold the player's shoulders there

vertex_colour: The land (payo_land_*: TWO materials, py_ground_grass tiling at 4 m with its forest shade in vertex colour, and py_rock on steep faces and the stream's bed), the terrace kit's stone, ground and plants, the life figures, the trees' solid parts and the kept far pieces carry vertex colour (COLOR_0) that their materials must multiply by; see `vertex_colour` per material in materials_payo.json. The painted single pieces (stone, gate, bulul, houses, props) do not need it.

terrace_lod.note: Every terrace placement has `lod` (by its distance from the 44 m play square: full under `full_under`, mid under `mid_under`, far beyond; `far` true) and `span` (metres of wall it stands for). A 12 m placement's three levels share pivot, footprint and curve: full is the bare name, mid is <name>_mid (with the spout's fall; about one in five) or <name>_mid_plain, far is <name>_far. FAR ROWS ARE MERGED: a run of straight far modules of one crop is ONE placement of <name>_far24 (span 24) or <name>_far48 (span 48), same pivot (the run's first module) and yaw; these have no full or mid form, so do not swap them by distance. Caps exist only full: a far row has no cap. Far material py_terrace_far_wall is new; a far flooded module's water is the object named *_water on the far atlas (py_terrace_far).

far_note: payo_range_1..5 are five separate pieces at 0.6, 1.0, 1.4, 2.0 and 2.7 km, all in the forest floor's material (py_ground; the nearest's terrace steps in py_grass): the game's distance fog must pale them one after another, as the review pictures' haze does. payo_clouds is the sea of cloud at y -50 out to 3.4 km. They are the draft's ranges brought to 0.56 of their distance and size. KEPT from the rejected pass (they were not the complaint) with their old materials py_ground, py_grass and py_cloud.
look: DAY (first half): a clear highland morning, the sun out over the valley to the north east at about 30 degrees, neutral to slightly warm key so the stone stays GREY, pale blue distance fog from about 120 m that takes the ranges one after another, cloud lying in the valley 50 m under the court. NIGHT (from half time): moonlight from the valley side, deep blue fog, warm fire light on the stage and the gate, Mayari over the far ridge.
notes: The pit: the wall kit runs from the lip (y -6) down 12 m to a ledge, at 30 m from the axis (the layout's pit); payo_pit_floor is that 4 m ledge and the dark shaft under it at 26 m.
Spout heads (bulul_spout) sit in the pit_wall_spout holes with a fall_medium at 0.62 under each, its pool on the ledge.
Falls are static pieces; py_fall's UV v runs downstream (scroll it). py_mist is the soft cloud at a fall's foot.
rope_bridge spans the stream bed south east of the court; its deck sags 0.58 m below its pivot.

TREES: the approved pieces have none, so the forest, palms, banana and bushes are the earlier Payo set's own models (tree_fig_*, tree_pine_*, payo_plant_*), kept with their old materials and textures; group 'plant' (they sway).
The great fall stands at the head of a gorge cut straight up the south field's western slope on bearing 202.92 from the can (it faces the can, yaw 22.92); the cliff kit lines both walls and the head.

THE STREAM runs down that one line: two small falls in the gorge, three medium falls down the hillside, one fall at each of the town's three benches, a runnel across the rim to the pit's spout at (-12, -30). No stream piece exists: the water is the falls' own pools; the land's vertex colour is wet rock along the bed.
THE TOWN stands on three benches of the south field (y -3.7, 0.9 and 5.5), the rows of rice between them; three rope bridges cross the stream.
A giant stands on its own platform ten walls up the east terraces (bulul_seated, scale 1.25) and the west (bulul_standing, 1.25).
THE KNOLL: a terraced hill with three houses 150 to 230 m north of the can, standing out of the cloud; payo_land_near_ne and _nw carry it.
